newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares ease, seen drifting until CA sale. [CORRECTED 15:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares ease, seen drifting until CA sale. [CORRECTED 15:35 GMT]

text.p: Austrian shares ended moderately lower on Tuesday and traders said they expect the market to drift sideways until a decision is made on the long-running sale of privatisation candidate Creditanstalt-Bankverein.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips fell 2.5 points (corrects from 0.71 points) to 1,137.09. Among its constituents 12 ATX shares rose and nine fell.

Preferred shares of Creditanstalt ended the day 4.5 schillings lower at 493 after Finance Minister Viktor Klima said he would make a decision on the sale of the flagship bank as soon as possible and accept only the highest offer.
Klima last week extended the tender to January 10 from a previous deadline of December 16 to allow the three bidders to boost their offers for the bank.
Preferred shares of Bank Austria, which has put in the highest offer for the state's stake in Creditanstalt, led the decliners, tumbling 2.17 percent to 405 schillings.

Traders attributed the fall to speculation that Bank Austria could lose its AAA rating if Klima chooses it as the buyer for Creditanstalt and agrees in return to take the bank out of the fold of the City of Vienna.

Bank Austria is controlled by the Social Democrat-dominated municipality but the conservative People's Party, the Social Democrats' junior coalition partner, is vehemently opposed to the sale of Creditanstalt to a "socialist" bank.
"If the community ceases to be liable for Bank Austria, then its AAA rating will be questionable," said one trader.
But traders said the mood on the Vienna bourse was fundamentally positive.
"Investors are holding back due to to the Creditanstalt deadline," said one trader. "If it all goes without any major problems, the market should go up," he added.
The session's top gainer was steelmaker VA Stahl, climbing 1.99 percent to 410 schillings.
The January ATX future shed 5.3 points to 1,135.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index lost 1.16 points or 0.27 percent to 427.68. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12257
